summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has moved to a SpaceX hangar in preparation for its upcoming launch, marking a key development for the next-generation observatory designed to directly image faint exoplanets and study cosmic evolution. In international civil space developments, Turkey is set to sign the Artemis Accords with NASA, while NASA astronaut Jonny Kim is departing the agency to return to active military service. Meanwhile, NASA's Swift space telescope is projected to reenter Earth’s atmosphere following the failure of a private rescue mission. In launch and commercial activity, Europe successfully launched a weather satellite aboard an Ariane 6 rocket, while SpaceX completed Falcon 9 Starlink missions, loaded a floating Starship spacecraft onto a vessel in the Indian Ocean, and announced plans for a new spaceport in Louisiana. In military space affairs, the U.S. Space Force adopted a digital engineering tool for its NC3 satellite program, awarded a $20.68 million contract to LeoLabs for its Scout initiative, and announced plans to evaluate commercial technology integration using a new scorecard system, while Canadian firms partnered on a Space Domain Awareness satellite solution. In space science, astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope ruled out two potential Dyson sphere candidates while gathering data on stellar planet formation, and researchers detected a thermal anomaly beneath Mars’ south pole. Looking ahead, observers should watch for tonight’s partial lunar eclipse, which will turn the moon an eerie red for millions of viewers.
